title: Reader: semaphore drain as shutdown barrier
description: After SIGTERM/CTRL-C, main() clones the semaphore before the select! loop, then calls semaphore_drain.acquire_many(max_connections) to block until all in-flight session tasks have released their owned permits. This is correct because the semaphore already serves as the connection-count enforcer, so draining it to zero is a direct proof that all sessions have exited — no separate tracking structure is needed. Alternative rejected: tokio_util CancellationToken broadcast plus JoinSet::join_all. That approach requires adding the tokio-util dependency, threading the token into every session task, and explicitly joining each handle. The semaphore approach reuses state that already exists and adds zero new imports or types.
